skill.name: nestjs-architecture-principles
skill.description: Designs and reviews NestJS application architecture using cohesive feature modules, modular monoliths, layered or hexagonal boundaries, dependency inversion, and pragmatic engineering principles. Use when planning a NestJS project, changing module boundaries, evaluating Clean Architecture or DDD, resolving circular dependencies, defining ports and adapters, reviewing coupling, or deciding whether CQRS or microservices are justified. Do not use for pure frontend work or non-NestJS backends. When other skills also apply, reconcile ownership before mutation.
skill.summary: Design and review NestJS module boundaries, dependency direction, data ownership, and incremental architecture changes.
skill.author: amirtaherkhani

content.value_statement: Unclear module boundaries make NestJS changes harder to test and coordinate. This skill guides evidence-based architecture decisions, explicit ownership, and incremental boundary repairs.
actual_capabilities: Guide architecture selection across feature modules, selective layering, hexagonal boundaries, CQRS, and independently deployed services.
Review module imports, provider exports, dependency direction, and circular dependencies against repository evidence.
Define application-owned ports, runtime provider tokens, adapter wiring, and appropriate provider lifetimes.
Assess data ownership, transaction scope, migration compatibility, and reliable event publication boundaries.
Produce architecture reviews with evidence, impact, minimal remedies, migration steps, and validation checks.
Evaluate service extraction using deployment, ownership, scaling, data, and failure requirements.
limitations: Targets NestJS backends rather than frontend applications or unrelated backend frameworks.
Provides instructions and reference examples, not a standalone architecture scanner or migration runner.
Requires repository access and concrete requirements to support evidence-based recommendations.
Does not prove runtime correctness, database behavior, or performance without relevant tests and measurements.

use_cases.title: Plan a new backend
use_cases.description: Choose cohesive feature modules, public operations, and data owners before adding layers or separate services.
use_cases.target_user: Backend developers starting a NestJS application

use_cases.title: Review an existing system
use_cases.description: Identify cross-feature write leaks, broad exports, and dependency cycles, then recommend focused repairs with regression checks.
use_cases.target_user: Technical leads reviewing maintainability and correctness

use_cases.title: Evaluate service extraction
use_cases.description: Compare worker scaling with business-service extraction and define ownership, contracts, consistency, and operational requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan feature modules
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a NestJS order-management API for one team and one deployment. Recommend module boundaries, public APIs, data ownership, and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Review module boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this NestJS repository without editing files. Map imports and exports, identify ownership violations, and report evidence, impact, minimal remedies, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a cycle repair
prompt_templates.prompt: OrdersModule and PaymentsModule depend on each other. Trace the workflow and propose an incremental cycle repair that preserves contracts and required consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate distributed boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate extracting reporting from our NestJS monolith. Compare worker deployment and microservices using ownership, scaling, data, failure, contracts, migration, and validation.

output_examples.input: A small team needs one NestJS deployment for an order-management API.
output: Decision: use a modular monolith with cohesive Orders, Catalog, and Billing capabilities.
Boundaries: each capability owns its writes and exposes only required application operations.
Trade-off: keep simple CRUD compact and layer only features with meaningful domain or integration complexity.
Validation: test public operations, module wiring, and forbidden cross-feature persistence imports.

output_examples.input: Orders and Payments have a circular dependency and both use forwardRef.
output: Baseline: trace the shared workflow and establish which capability owns its invariant.
Decision: consider an owning coordinator or narrow port before asynchronous events.
Migration: characterize behavior, move callers incrementally, then remove temporary circular wiring.
Validation: compile affected modules and verify payment failures preserve the required order invariant.

output_examples.input: A CPU-heavy report generator needs more capacity than the rest of the application.
output: Decision: evaluate a separately scaled worker before creating a business microservice.
Boundary: define job identity, idempotency, retry limits, payload bounds, and data access ownership.
Extraction gate: require evidence of independent operation and account for contract and failure costs.
Validation: test duplicate jobs, partial failures, backlog limits, and shutdown behavior.

best_practices: Inspect installed versions, module wiring, callers, tests, and concrete change pressures before choosing an architecture.
Assign clear capability and write ownership, then add only boundaries justified by current requirements.
Make changes incrementally, preserve public contracts, and verify boundaries with existing lint, module, integration, or contract tests.
anti_patterns: Introduce CQRS, microservices, or strict layering only to match a preferred diagram.
Export every provider or let features directly write another capability's tables.
Treat forwardRef as the default cycle repair or create interfaces for every stable local helper.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It guides NestJS architecture selection, module boundaries, dependency injection, data ownership, and evidence-based reviews.

faq.question: Does every NestJS application need Clean Architecture?
faq.answer: No. It starts with cohesive feature modules and recommends selective layers only when domain complexity or infrastructure changes justify them.

faq.question: Does it require other NestJS skills?
faq.answer: No. Related skills are optional coordination partners with distinct ownership boundaries.

faq.question: Can it fix circular dependencies?
faq.answer: It guides ownership analysis and incremental repairs using coordinators, narrow ports, or events when consistency requirements permit.

faq.question: Does it automatically run migrations or verify performance?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and validation plans; real database behavior and performance require appropriate tests and measurements.

faq.question: When does it recommend microservices?
faq.answer: Only when concrete deployment, ownership, scaling, data, or failure boundaries justify independent operation and its added costs.
